textbookText: crucial in clarifying phylogenetic uncertainties, such as the classification of the king crab (Limulus), where antigens from various arthropods were tested against Limulus serum, confirming its placement in the Arachnida class. Similarly, comparative serological tests have resolved uncertainties among mammals, such as the relationship between whales and fishes. Despite morphological similarities, serological tests show that whale serum proteins are most like those of even-toed hoofed mammals, suggesting their evolution from a primitive artiodactyla stock. Comparative serology among primates, including man, anthropoid apes, monkeys, lemurs, and dogs, revealed an increasing order of precipitate formation, indicating the closest relationship between man and anthropoid apes. c. Enzymes and Hormones: Remarkable similarities in digestive enzymes such as Trypsin, Lipase, amylase, etc. and hormones are observed in large groups of animals. This further supports organic evolution.

9. What field of study provides strong evidence supporting the theory of organic evolution by comparing the early stages of animal development? a. Palaeontology b. Embryology c. Biochemistry d. Comparative physiology

10. What is the primary function of serological tests in understanding evolutionary relationships between different organisms? a. Determining the age of fossils b. 11. Which theory, proposed by Ernst Haeckel, suggests that the developmental history of an organism repeats its ancestral history? a. Recapitulation Theory b. Ontogeny Theory c. Phylogenetic Theory d. Evolutionary Recapitulation
